title: Inverse formulas for any insertion-normalized sheaf scalar tensor map
statement:
Let $D$ be a site small in a common ring and module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $A,S$ be sheaves of commutative rings on $D$, and let $\alpha:A\to S$ be a unital ring-sheaf morphism. Let $H,K$ be sheaves of $A$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an $A$-module sheaf $X$, put
$$T(X)=\bigl(U\longmapsto S(U)\otimes_{A(U)}X(U)\bigr)^\#,$$
using module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Write $\tau_X(s,x)$ for the sheafification image of $s\otimes x$ and $q_X(x)=\tau_X(1,x)$. All tensor products of sheaves are sheafified balanced tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

Let $b:T(H\otimes_AK)\to T(H)\otimes_ST(K)$ be any $S$-linear sheaf map satisfying, for every $U\in D$, $h\in H(U)$ and $k\in K(U)$,
$$b\bigl(q_{H\otimes_AK}(h\otimes k)\bigr)=q_H(h)\otimes q_K(k).$$
Then $b$ is an isomorphism, and for all $s,t\in S(U)$ its forward and inverse section formulas are
$$b\bigl(\tau_{H\otimes_AK}(s,h\otimes k)\bigr)=\tau_H(s,h)\otimes\tau_K(1,k),$$
$$b^{-1}\bigl(\tau_H(s,h)\otimes\tau_K(t,k)\bigr)
=\tau_{H\otimes_AK}(st,h\otimes k).$$
The inverse is an $S$-linear morphism of sheaves. No flatness or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor, and section-tensor-product; agent balanced inverse calculation in original item Step 4.

proof.text:
Put $L=H\otimes_AK$, $V=T(L)$ and $W=T(H)\otimes_ST(K)$. Write $P_X(U)=S(U)\otimes_{A(U)}X(U)$ and $\iota_X:P_X\to T(X)$ for its $S$-linear sheafification unit. The balancing relation gives $q_X(ax)=\tau_X(1,ax)=\tau_X(\alpha(a),x)=\alpha(a)q_X(x)$, so $q_X:X\to\operatorname{Res}_\alpha T(X)$ is $A$-linear. Since $\tau_X(s,x)=s q_X(x)$, the given normalization and $S$-linearity of $b$ imply
$$b(\tau_L(s,h\otimes k))=s(q_H(h)\otimes q_K(k))=\tau_H(s,h)\otimes\tau_K(1,k).$$
This proves the forward formula without any assertion about generation of sheaf sections.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor) and Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); agent explicit balanced inverse calculation.

proof.text:
For each $U$ define a pairing $\beta_U:P_H(U)\times P_K(U)\to V(U)$ on pure tensors by
$$\beta_U(s\otimes h,t\otimes k)=\tau_L(st,h\otimes k).$$
This descends through both ordinary tensor products by their universal property: the displayed expression is additive separately in $s,h,t,k$; for $a\in A(U)$ its two balancing checks are
$$\tau_L(s\alpha(a)t,h\otimes k)=\tau_L(st,(ah)\otimes k),\qquad
\tau_L(st\alpha(a),h\otimes k)=\tau_L(st,h\otimes(ak)).$$
Indeed, in the first equality move $\alpha(a)$ across the scalar-extension tensor, then use $a(h\otimes k)=(ah)\otimes k$; in the second use $a(h\otimes k)=h\otimes(ak)$. Commutativity of $S(U)$ and scalar linearity of $\iota_L$ give
$$\beta_U(r(s\otimes h),t\otimes k)=r\beta_U(s\otimes h,t\otimes k)=\beta_U(s\otimes h,r(t\otimes k)).$$
Additivity extends these identities from pure tensors to finite sums, which generate the ordinary tensor products. Thus $\beta_U$ is $S(U)$-bilinear. In Lean, use TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange.symm, followed by scalar extension of the sheaf-tensor unit and the scalar sheafification unit, to implement this pairing without quotient calculations.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor) and Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); agent explicit balanced inverse calculation.

proof.text:
For $f:U'\to U$, naturality of the pure tensor maps and $\iota_L$ gives
$$\beta_U(s\otimes h,t\otimes k)|_{U'}=\tau_L(s|_{U'}t|_{U'},h|_{U'}\otimes k|_{U'})=\beta_{U'}((s\otimes h)|_{U'},(t\otimes k)|_{U'}).$$
Ordinary tensor generation extends this equality to all pairs of sections of $P_H,P_K$. Hence the pairings of Step 2 form a morphism of presheaves of sets $\beta:P_H\times P_K\to V$, bilinear over the ring sheaf $S$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor) and Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); agent explicit balanced inverse calculation.

proof.text:
Apply the bilinear-extension theorem with ring presheaf $\mathcal O=S$, already a sheaf, with $\mathcal F=P_H$, $\mathcal G=P_K$ and target $\mathcal H=V$. All modules and the site lie in the common universe of the statement. It gives a unique $S$-bilinear sheaf pairing $\beta^\#:T(H)\times T(K)\to V$ extending $\beta$. The sheaf tensor universal property over $S$ now gives an $S$-linear sheaf morphism $d:W\to V$ with
$$d(\tau_H(s,h)\otimes\tau_K(t,k))=\tau_L(st,h\otimes k).$$
Here the input is the canonical pure tensor of the two sheaf sections; no surjectivity on sections of a sheafification unit is needed. For the direct sheafification object siteSheafTensorRight, implement the cited tensor universal property directly using TensorProduct.lift and the Mathlib module-sheafification adjunction (private tensorLift and tensorLift_apply); no transport to the localization tensor is needed.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor) and Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); agent explicit balanced inverse calculation.

proof.text:
We prove $db=\mathrm{id}_V$. The module sheafification universal property for $P_L\to V$ reduces equality of these $S$-linear maps to equality after $\iota_L$. Sectionwise, $P_L(U)$ is generated by $s\otimes x$ and $\tau_L(s,x)=s q_L(x)$, so it suffices to prove equality of the $A$-linear sheaf maps $dbq_L,q_L:L\to\operatorname{Res}_\alpha V$. The sheaf tensor universal property over $A$ reduces that equality to $x=h\otimes k$, for all objects and sections. There the normalization and Step 4 give
$$dbq_L(h\otimes k)=d(q_H(h)\otimes q_K(k))=\tau_L(1,h\otimes k)=q_L(h\otimes k).$$
Both reductions are injectivity/uniqueness assertions of the cited universal properties, so they establish equality on all sheaf sections. The direct tensor uniqueness assertion is the private proved tensor_ext, obtained from the sheafification adjunction and TensorProduct.ext'.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor) and Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); agent explicit balanced inverse calculation.

proof.text: For bd=id_W, direct tensor uniqueness reduces equality to the two natural S-bilinear families obtained by composing the pure tensor pairing with bd and with id_W. Apply unique_bilinear_sheafification_extension to reduce to the two presheaf units. Tensor induction in both presheaf arguments and S-bilinearity reduce further to the pair (1 tensor h,1 tensor k): each s tensor h is s times 1 tensor h, and the same holds for the other argument. On this pair, the inverse formula gives d(q_H(h) tensor q_K(k))=tau_L(1,h tensor k); the normalization of b sends this to q_H(h) tensor q_K(k). This proves bd=id_W. Together with the first identity, the already constructed S-linear morphism d is b inverse and has the asserted scalar-multiplying formula. The private scalarTensor_ext implements precisely this uniqueness and scalar-generation argument; it does not assume that sheafification units are surjective on sections. Zero rings, arbitrary ring maps and arbitrary module sheaves are included.
